countries.name: Bangladesh
countries.summary: Bangladesh is a well-established South Asian destination for English-medium MBBS study, with government-regulated, University-of-Dhaka-affiliated medical colleges recognized by the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council. Its direct-entry, five-year MBBS plus one-year internship structure closely mirrors the route familiar to Indian and Nepali applicants.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: Proximity to India and Nepal keeps travel and living costs manageable, while English-medium instruction and a BMDC-regulated, University-of-Dhaka-affiliated MBBS structure offer a familiar five-year direct-entry route plus a compulsory one-year rotatory internship. Government-coordinated foreign-student admissions add a standardized, centrally verified application process across recognized colleges.
countries.climate: Subtropical monsoon climate with a hot, humid summer, a monsoon season from June to October bringing heavy rainfall, and a mild, dry winter from November to February.

universities.name: Bangladesh Medical College
universities.summary: Bangladesh Medical College is a private medical college in Dhaka founded in 1986, a constituent college of the University of Dhaka since 1988. Its five-year MBBS programme is recognized by the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council, listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools, and its graduates are ECFMG-certification eligible, with English-medium teaching and an attached 600-bed teaching hospital.
universities.campusLifestyle: The Dhanmondi campus houses four air-conditioned lecture classrooms with full WiFi, around 30 departmental tutorial rooms, eight subject laboratories, an air-conditioned Anatomy Dissection Hall, and an air-conditioned library seating 110 students with roughly 7,754 books and seven international medical journal subscriptions, alongside a 250-seat auditorium and separate common rooms.
universities.cityProfile: Bangladesh Medical College sits in Dhanmondi, a central institutional district of Dhaka, Bangladesh's capital. The college's own admission circular places its government-set intake at 120 seats per year, with foreign-student admission capped at 45 percent of a college's total allocated seats under national policy. The attached Bangladesh Medical College Hospital anchors clinical training within the same Dhanmondi campus.
universities.practicalExposure: Clinical training runs through the college's own attached Bangladesh Medical College Hospital, a 600-bed teaching hospital with 217 general beds, 293 paid beds, 31 cabins and 60 free beds, including a Community Welfare and Health Care Centre building, an Outpatient Department, a Modern Accident and Emergency Department and its own oxygen plant. Named clinical departments include Gynae and Obstetrics, Cardiology, Dermatology, ENT, Gastroenterology, Endocrinology, Nephrology, Neuro Medicine, Ophthalmology, Orthopedic Surgery, Paediatrics, Neurosurgery, Psychiatry, Radiology and Imaging, Radiotherapy and Oncology, Urology, Transfusion Medicine, Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine. The five academic years, organized into four professional phases, are followed by a compulsory one-year logbook-based rotatory internship that must be completed within twelve years of first admission.
universities.hostelOverview: The college operates a Dhanmondi hostel with furnished rooms, free WiFi, washing machine, refrigerator, TV, 24-hour security, a 24-hour attendant and CCTV coverage. Published foreign-student monthly rates run from USD 160 for non-AC rooms up to USD 190 for a single AC room, with double and triple AC rooms priced between.
universities.dietarySupport: Food service is included among the hostel facilities, though no separate mess-fee figure is published. Because the college's official tuition figure for foreign students is unavailable, daily food and living costs should be planned as a distinct budget line pending a direct fee quote from the college.
universities.safetyOverview: The college's hostel facilities include 24-hour security service, a 24-hour attendant and CCTV coverage. No dedicated international-student safety office or emergency-contact programme is separately published on official pages reviewed.
universities.studentSupport: Foreign-student admission is coordinated centrally through the Government of Bangladesh's Directorate General of Medical Education (DGME) online portal, which sets the eligibility criteria, application window and seat allocation that Bangladesh Medical College follows for its foreign intake.
whyChoose: A constituent college of the University of Dhaka since 1988, with a multi-decade international-recognition track record including WHO World Directory of Medical Schools listing and ECFMG Certification eligibility for graduates since 1989.
Recognized by the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council and confirmed on the government's Directorate General of Medical Education foreign-student admission circular.
English-medium MBBS instruction confirmed by the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools.
An attached 600-bed teaching hospital, Bangladesh Medical College Hospital, spanning a broad range of named specialty departments for direct clinical exposure.
Transparently published, itemized monthly hostel rates for foreign students, ranging from USD 160 to USD 190.
thingsToConsider: No official source currently publishes a foreign-student tuition figure; the government's own admission circular directs applicants to obtain a fee quote directly from the college, and the college's live website was unreachable during recent research -- get written confirmation before committing.
Foreign-student seats are capped at 45 percent of the college's total allocated seats under Bangladesh government policy; meeting eligibility criteria does not guarantee a seat.

Indian applicants must separately satisfy India's own NEET-UG and National Medical Commission eligibility requirements, managed entirely by Indian authorities and independent of the college's own admission process.
The foreign-student eligibility and deadline rules are reissued each academic session by the Bangladesh government; confirm the current session's exact criteria and dates before applying.

faq.question: Is Bangladesh Medical College recognized by BMDC and the WHO?
faq.answer: Yes. It is listed on the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council's official register of colleges and enlisted in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools, FAIMER School ID F0000244, with operational status currently operational.

faq.question: Is Bangladesh Medical College affiliated with a public university?
faq.answer: Yes. It is a constituent college of the University of Dhaka, an affiliation dating from 10 May 1988, confirmed on both the college's own site and Dhaka University's own constituent-colleges portal.

faq.question: How long is the MBBS programme?
faq.answer: 5 years of academic study divided into four professional phases, followed by a mandatory 1-year logbook-based rotatory internship, to be completed within 12 years of first admission.

faq.question: What language is the MBBS programme taught in?
faq.answer: English, confirmed by the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools and the college's own curriculum documentation.

faq.question: When does the academic session start?
faq.answer: The academic year starts in January. Government foreign-student admission circulars run on an annual cycle; the most recently published cycle took applications from November through mid-January, with admission formalities continuing into February.

faq.question: What are the eligibility requirements for foreign applicants, including Indian students?
faq.answer: O-level/equivalent with a science background and A-level/equivalent with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, an aggregate GPA of at least 7.0 (5-point scale) in each, and at least 3.50 in Biology at A-level, per Bangladesh's national foreign-student admission circular.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to enroll?
faq.answer: This is a separate, India-side requirement governed by India's National Medical Commission, not by Bangladesh Medical College. Applicants should confirm the current rule directly with NMC before applying.

faq.question: What is the tuition fee for foreign students?
faq.answer: Not currently published on any official source; the Bangladesh government's own admission circular directs applicants to obtain fee information directly from the college.

faq.question: Is hostel accommodation available for foreign students?
faq.answer: Yes. The college publishes foreign-student hostel rates ranging from USD 160 per month for non-AC rooms to USD 190 for a single AC room, with furnished rooms, WiFi and 24-hour security.

faq.question: Which hospital do students train at?
faq.answer: Bangladesh Medical College Hospital, a 600-bed teaching hospital attached to the college in Dhanmondi, with named departments spanning Cardiology, Orthopedic Surgery, Neurosurgery, Radiotherapy and Oncology, and more.

admissionsContent.overview: International admission is coordinated centrally through the Government of Bangladesh's DGME online portal, with eligibility, application windows and a foreign-student seat cap set nationally; Bangladesh Medical College follows this same government process rather than running a separate foreign-admissions track of its own.

eligibility.intro: Foreign applicants need O-level (science background) and A-level or equivalent HSC in Physics, Chemistry and Biology, with an aggregate GPA of at least 7.0 on a 5-point scale and at least 3.50 in Biology at A-level, per the current government foreign-student circular.
items: A-level/equivalent with Physics, Chemistry and Biology
Aggregate GPA of at least 7.0 (5-point scale) in each of O-level and A-level
Biology grade point of at least 3.50 at A-level, with no single subject below 3.50
Indian applicants: current NEET-UG qualification per India's National Medical Commission rules, separate from Bangladesh's own admission process

applicationSteps: Apply online via the Government of Bangladesh's foreignstudents.dgme.gov.bd portal within the announced window
Upload a passport photo, passport copy, and Ministry-attested O-level/A-level certificates and mark sheets
Remit the non-refundable USD 100 equivalence fee by telegraphic transfer or SWIFT and upload proof of payment
Collect a printed copy of the submitted application from the online portal
If selected, submit original certificates, mark sheets and transcripts to the college's Principal's office by the government-set admission deadline

academic: A-level/HSC-equivalent certificate and mark sheet (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
application: Online application in the government portal's specified template
Proof of USD 100 telegraphic transfer/SWIFT payment
Passport copy and recent passport-size photograph
Home-country Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation on academic documents

admissionsContent.deadlinesNote: The most recently published cycle ran 11 November 2025 to 15 January 2026 for applications, with college-level admission continuing to 19 February 2026; confirm the current session's exact dates with the government DGME portal before applying.
visaConsiderations: Foreign applicants are admitted through Bangladesh's centralized government DGME process rather than a college-specific visa track; confirm current visa requirements with the college and portal.
